text:
And I moved my vigorous traveler's legs
and stretched toward the blue mountain.
I carried the whole night on my Atlantean back.
The stars sang for me.


Dawn broke on the river and I crossed it naked
and, dripping the dawn, I cleft the whole mountain.
And it was the dark taste of raw cacao
when, chewing, the tapir's teeth grind it.


The light asked for a hollow to settle its account
(I carried a handful of dawn inside me).
The cedars tightened their distance, and violently
the shadow gathered the ray of light I split.


Upon the dead leaves of a hundred centuries, I camp.
I come from the mountain and made the blue sprout again.
I arch the field's horizontal into a clear circle.
The whole body I raised rises over my legs.


It surrounds the valley. I speak,
and life all around knows what I know.

translation.title: The Journey
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish rendering. The Atlantean burden, dawn crossing, cacao/tapir taste, and final expansive identification with the valley are preserved.
